parts.title: About this guide and exam strategy

points.text: Exam overview and domain guide (Parts 1 and 3): exam format, weightings, and detailed technical chapters.
Troubleshooting, Integrations, and Architecture together make up 64% of the exam.
Read sections 2 to 9 in order, then use section 10 to check each question.
at.js is the client library that runs Target requests and applies experiences.
The key question for each method: where does the data come from, and is it stored in the visitor profile?
targetPageParams() supplies page-level parameters to the global mbox before the request is sent.
One Target installation can serve several business units.
at_property holds the property token, a unique ID string for one property.
Product page entity.categoryId takes a comma-separated list: one product, several categories.
Profile scripts are JavaScript snippets defined in Target.
Debugging: use mboxTrace to compare profile values before and after a profile script runs (Q45, Q46).
Experience Targeting: one winning experience per visitor, chosen by audience.
Experience: what the visitor sees, built in the Visual Experience Composer (VEC).
Client-side (at.js): the browser library.
Recommendations uses a catalog built from feeds, collections, or Analytics classifications.
Product feeds (Google Product Feeds): reuse organic search product data and automate inclusion (Q26).
Product page: entity.categoryId takes a comma-separated list.
A4T (Analytics for Target) sends Target results into Analytics.
iOS targeted locations: the two primary methods are targetLoadRequest and targetCreateRequestWithName (Q29).
Day 1: page-load order and execution (Q2, Q4, Q11, Q22, Q43, Q49), then mbox parameters and at_property (Q17, Q21, Q23, Q25, Q27, Q30, Q33 to Q36, Q48).
Adobe Target is Adobe’s personalization and experimentation platform.
Analytics for Target (A4T) sends Target activity and experience data into Adobe Analytics.
Access is managed through Adobe Admin Console product profiles and Target permissions .
at.js is the legacy client library.
Overview: Recommendations return ranked items (products, articles, offers) for a visitor, based on the item catalog, criteria, and algorithm.
Separate decisioning from content: Target decides which experience to show.
Troubleshooting is the largest domain.
